diveTitle: What actually happens when you redact
diveSubtitle: What gets removed from the file, and what stays.
dive1Title: Why a black box alone isn't real redaction
dive1Desc: Many free tools just draw an opaque rectangle over content — the text underneath is completely intact and can be recovered by selecting it, copying it, or opening the PDF in an editor. This is a well-documented category of real-world data leaks.
dive2Desc: We rasterize the redacted region — converting it into a flat image and overwriting the actual pixel data with black — rather than layering a shape on top. There's no underlying text object left to extract; the original content is genuinely gone from that area.
dive3Title: Can redacted text still be found with search?
dive3Desc: No. Because the underlying text object is destroyed, not hidden, a text search (Ctrl+F) finds nothing where the redaction was — there's no text left to match, which is exactly the point.
dive4Title: Redacting text vs. images vs. both
dive4Desc: The same rasterize-and-burn approach works whether you're redacting a paragraph of text, a photo, a signature, or any other visual element on the page — the tool doesn't distinguish between content types when applying the redaction.
dive5Desc: Not from the redacted file itself, by design — that's the whole point of true redaction. If you need the original content back, you'd need your original, pre-redaction copy of the document.
dive6Title: Does redaction also clean the document metadata?
dive6Desc: Redaction handles the visible page content specifically. Document metadata — author name, creation software, revision history — is a separate layer and isn't automatically stripped by redacting page content, so review your document's properties separately if metadata is also a concern.
faq1A: Yes. We rasterize the pages you redact and burn the selected areas black, so the underlying text and images are permanently removed from the file. They cannot be recovered by copy-paste, select-all, or a PDF editor.
faq2Q: How is this different from drawing a black box?
faq2A: A drawn black box only covers the content visually — the original text is still stored in the PDF and can be extracted. Our tool destroys the actual pixels, so nothing remains underneath.
faq3Q: Will the rest of my document change?
faq3A: Only the pages you redact are converted to images (they stay visually identical). Pages with no redaction boxes are left untouched and remain selectable and searchable.
faq4Q: Is it safe to upload my PDF?
faq4A: Yes. Files are sent over an encrypted connection, scanned for malware, and automatically deleted from our servers within 1 hour.
faq5Q: Can I redact a password-protected PDF?
faq5A: Please unlock the PDF first using our Unlock PDF tool, then redact the unlocked file.
